title: Exact quasi-coherent algebra direct image for affine stack morphisms
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $q:\mathcal U\to\mathcal X$ be a morphism of algebraic stacks over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Suppose $q$ is affine, meaning that for every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$ the $2$-fibre product $\mathcal U_T$ is a scheme and its projection to $T$ is affine [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Quasi-coherent algebras, their surjections and global sections have the meaning of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Then there is a functor $q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}$ from quasi-coherent commutative algebras on $\mathcal U$ to those on $\mathcal X$, right adjoint to tensor pullback, characterized on every smooth scheme test $T\to\mathcal X$ by ordinary affine pushforward from $\mathcal U_T$ to $T$. Smooth means [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] on scheme charts. This functor takes surjections to surjections, and there are natural ring isomorphisms $$\Gamma(\mathcal X,q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal A)\cong\Gamma(\mathcal U,\mathcal A).$$ They commute with algebra homomorphisms, multiplication and powers. In particular a lift of a power in the left-hand global section rings corresponds to the same power lift in the right-hand rings. Moreover, if $R\to S$ is any homomorphism of commutative $k$-algebras and $\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ any morphism, the projection $\mathcal X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}S\to\mathcal X$ is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. No Noetherian, finite-type, or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GQY (lemma-quasi-coherent-pushforward-affine), exactness of the quasi-coherent right adjoint; Tag 077A (proposition-direct-image-quasi-coherent) and Tag 0GQQ (lemma-direct-image-quasi-coherent-over-flat) give its adjunction and smooth-chart description. Algebra structures use Tag 0GQR (remark-direct-image-quasi-coherent-tensor); global sections use the pullback adjunction and the canonical identification of pulled-back structure sheaves. Stack affine base change: stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 0CHR (lemma-base-change-affine); scheme/algebra equivalence on affine charts: morphisms.tex Tag 01SA (lemma-affine-equivalence-algebras).

proof.text: For a scheme test $x:T\to\mathcal X$, put $V_x=\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal X}T$ and $f_x:V_x\to T$. These are a scheme and an affine morphism by the hypothesis on $q$. Restrict $\mathcal A$ along $V_x\to\mathcal U$ and use [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] to obtain an ordinary quasi-coherent algebra $A_x$ on $V_x$. The algebra operations come from the fully faithful, tensor-compatible comparison. For an arrow $x'\to x$ over $h:T'\to T$, the triples defining the $2$-fibre products identify $V_{x'}$ with $V_x\times_TT'$, and the same restriction lemma identifies $A_{x'}$ with the pullback of $A_x$. All these identifications satisfy composition, since they send a triple and its isomorphism to the same triple.

Set $M_x=(f_x)_*A_x$ as an ordinary module on $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] it is quasi-coherent, and for every arrow $x'\to x$ there is the canonical isomorphism $h^*M_x\simeq M_{x'}$. Its clause (3) supplies composition compatibility; for an identity its displayed tensor formula is the identity. Apply [lem-sfb-cartesian-module-fppf-realization] to this system. It gives a quasi-coherent sheaf $B$ on $\mathcal X$ with $B(x)=\Gamma(T,M_x)=\Gamma(V_x,A_x)$ and restrictions given by pullback of sections. Give $B(x)$ the ring operations of $\Gamma(V_x,A_x)$ and its $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$-algebra structure via $f_x$. Restrictions preserve these operations, so this is a quasi-coherent commutative algebra. Algebra homomorphisms $\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ induce the section maps, giving the functor $q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}$. On the slice over $x$, its values are exactly those associated with $M_x$, by the displayed base-change isomorphisms. Thus its ordinary restriction to $T$ is $(f_x)_*A_x$, for every scheme test and in particular every smooth test. This also specifies its algebra structure, since restrictions preserve products and the unit.

source.place: 06WK cartesian realization; coherent.tex 02KG (lemma-affine-base-change), including the canonical tensor formulas

proof.text: For a quasi-coherent algebra $D$ on $\mathcal X$, tensor pullback along $q$ is precomposition: $(q^*D)(u)=D(q(u))$ by [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction]. Given an algebra map $b:D\to B$, define $c_u:D(q(u))\to\mathcal A(u)$ by $b_{q(u)}$ followed by restriction along the graph $T\to V_{q(u)}$ of $u:T\to\mathcal U$. Conversely, from $c:q^*D\to\mathcal A$, define $b_x(d)$ as follows. For every $v:W\to V_x$, restrict $d\in D(x)$ along $f_xv:W\to T$ and apply $c$ at the induced object $W\to\mathcal U$. These sections are compatible with every arrow over $V_x$, hence give a section of $A_x$ by the scheme-test comparison. The two recipes are inverse: in one direction evaluation at the graph returns $c_u(d)$; in the other, naturality of $b$ along $q(u)\to x$ identifies its restriction to each $W\to V_x$ with the original section $b_x(d)|_W$. They preserve addition, multiplication, the unit, and structural scalars because restriction and $c$, respectively $b$, do. The formulas also commute with maps in $D$ and $\mathcal A$. They give the required natural algebra adjunction $q^*\dashv q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}$.

source.place: 06WH (pullback as precomposition), 06WI and 03DX (scheme-test comparison); explicit adjunct formulas

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal A'$ be a surjection of quasi-coherent algebras. For each $x:T\to\mathcal X$, scheme-test restriction gives a surjection $A_x\twoheadrightarrow A'_x$ of ordinary quasi-coherent modules on $V_x$. Its kernel $K_x$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. The quotient $A_x/K_x$ identifies with $A'_x$: locally a target section lifts, and any two lifts differ by $K_x$. Apply [lem-trf-affine-pushforward-quasi-coherent-quotient] to $(A_x,K_x)$ and the affine morphism $f_x$. It says that $(f_x)_*A_x\to(f_x)_*A'_x$ is surjective. By the converse surjection criterion of [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction], the map $B\to B'$ is a sheaf surjection. In fact sections lift on affine tests $T$, since then $V_x$ is affine and the same quotient lemma gives surjectivity on $\Gamma(V_x,-)$. This asserts no exactness of arbitrary global sections on $\mathcal X$.

source.place: 06WI and descent.tex 06VE for surjections; schemes.tex 01IC and divisors.tex 080G affine quotient calculation

proof.text: A global section $s$ of $\mathcal A$ restricts to each $V_x$ and hence gives a compatible family in $B(x)=\Gamma(V_x,A_x)$. Conversely, from a compatible family $t_x\in B(x)$, define its value at $u:T\to\mathcal U$ by restricting $t_{q(u)}$ along the graph $T\to V_{q(u)}$. Compatibility with arrows makes this a global section of $\mathcal A$. These maps are inverse: a restricted global section evaluates at the graph to its original value; for the other composite and each $v:W\to V_x$, compatibility along $q(u)\to x$, where $u:W\to\mathcal U$ is induced by $v$, says that graph evaluation is exactly $t_x|_W$. Sections are equal when their values at all objects are equal. By the definition of global sections as compatible families, this proves $\Gamma(\mathcal X,B)\simeq\Gamma(\mathcal U,\mathcal A)$. Every operation is restriction or evaluation, so the bijection is a ring isomorphism and is natural in algebra homomorphisms. In particular it sends $a^n$ to the $n$th power of the image of $a$ for every $n\geq0$. An equation $a\mapsto b^n$ therefore becomes exactly the same equation after applying the isomorphisms, proving the power-lift assertion.

source.place: Definition of global sections as compatible families; 06WI scheme-test comparison

proof.text: Finally let $R\to S$ be as in the statement. The scheme map $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. For any scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, the $2$-fibre product of $T$ with $\mathcal X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}S$ over $\mathcal X$ is $T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}S$: on objects one forgets the redundant $\mathcal X$ object using the specified isomorphism in the triple. It is a scheme by [def-pc-fibre-product], and its projection to $T$ is affine by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. This is precisely the representable-affine condition imposed in the item. The construction and the preceding steps used neither flatness nor Noetherian or finite-type hypotheses.

This is a first split, not a re-split: the base item had no proof and there is no repair note. The item statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and contain no SGA citation. New node lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction: checked against Stacks 06WK (proof: slice = (Sch/V)_fppf plus 03DX), 06WI, 06WH and descent 06VE parts 1, 3, 4 and 7. It correctly avoids the left exactness that 06VE(6) warns is false. I checked both surjection clauses by hand: the forward one via right exactness and Q^a=0 implying Q=0, the converse via affine-local lifting on a Zariski cover. No duplicate exists; lem-sfb-cartesian-module-fppf-realization is the converse construction and is reused in step 2. The node does not restate any clause of the item. Steps: (1) V_x, A_x and cartesian identifications via the new node; (2) M_x=(f_x)_*A_x with base change and composition from pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change (1)/(3), fed into the cartesian realization to give B with B(x)=Γ(V_x,A_x), and B_x=(f_x)_*A_x by uniqueness; (3) adjunction by graph evaluation and induced objects, both composites checked via naturality; (4) surjection via the kernel lemma, the affine quotient lemma and the new node's converse; (5) global sections as compatible families, giving a ring isomorphism that preserves powers; (6) T×_X(X×_R S)=T×_R S, affine by permanence (1). Step uses equal proof_deps, and there is no cycle with the adequately-affine citers. Advisory: lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-algebra-direct-image partly generalizes the adjoint clause, but lacks the surjection, global-section and scalar-change clauses and would need an affine-implies-qcqs lemma; the direct construction is correct. Batch 5: lem-trf-affine-pushforward-quasi-coherent-quotient is a generic scheme exactness lemma, not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so accepted. The def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids path to def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism and the def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra path to def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module both reach general definitions only, so accepted.
